    using stow to manage my collection of dotfiles more easily

# GNU Stow Cheatsheet for Dotfiles(Generated by AI)

This cheatsheet summarizes the basic commands and workflows for managing dotfiles with [GNU Stow](https://www.gnu.org/software/stow/).

---

## 📁 Directory Structure

Organize your dotfiles like this:

```

dotfiles/
├── alacritty/
│   └── .config/alacritty/
├── nvim/
│   └── .config/nvim/
├── zsh/
│   ├── .zshrc
│   └── .zprofile
├── vim/
│   └── .vimrc
└── ...

````

- Each subdirectory is a **package**.
- Paths inside each package mimic the **target location in `$HOME`**.

---

## ⚡ Stow Commands Reference

| Command | Description | Example |
|---------|------------|---------|
| `stow <package>` | Create symlinks for a package | `stow -t ~ nvim` |
| `stow -D <package>` | Remove symlinks for a package | `stow -D -t ~ zsh` |
| `stow -R <package>` | Restow (reapply) a package | `stow -R -t ~ tmux` |
| `stow */` | Stow all packages at once | `stow -t ~ */` |
| `stow -n <package>` | Dry-run; preview changes | `stow -n -t ~ picom` |
| `stow --adopt <package>` | Adopt existing files into stow | `stow --adopt -t ~ kitty` |

---

## 🔧 Tips

- Always run `stow` from the **root of your dotfiles repo**.
- Use `-t ~` to explicitly set `$HOME` as the target.
- Backup conflicting files before stowing to avoid accidental overwrites.
- Check symlinks with:

```bash
ls -l ~/.config/<app>
````

---

## 🛠 Example Workflow

```bash
# Move existing config into stow repo
mkdir -p ~/gitbuilds/dotfiles/picom/.config
mv ~/.config/picom ~/gitbuilds/dotfiles/picom/.config/

# Stow it
cd ~/gitbuilds/dotfiles
stow -t ~ picom

# Verify symlink
ls -l ~/.config/picom
# Output: ~/.config/picom -> ~/gitbuilds/dotfiles/picom/.config/picom
```

---

## 🔄 Bulk Adoption (Optional)

To adopt multiple configs already in `$HOME`:

```bash
stow --adopt -t ~ picom nvim zsh tmux
```
